# Kotoba context for AI agents

Kotoba is a Clojure-shaped language profile and computing stack designed for code written or operated by AI agents. Its security direction is explicit capability and effect confinement: source requests authority, policy can only narrow it, and the host binds only admitted providers. Kotoba complements compiler, runtime, provider, OS, and key-custody controls; it is not an "unhackable" claim.

Product defaults are machine-readable in `lang/product-defaults.edn`. The public language is post-quantum-by-default for new cryptographic boundaries, authentication-aware and authority-deny-by-default, attenuation-only for delegation, chain-neutral for linked Web3 accounts, and AI-agent-first. Zero-copy is bounded: uncompressed Arrow projection can retain CPU backing through the authorized Kotobase lake path. A non-nullable float32 column was observed retaining one ArrayBuffer through Arrow and its CPU typed view, then crossing to Num with one 16-byte WebGPU upload on Apple M4/Metal and returning one 4-byte scalar after device execution. Network ingress, decompression, GPU upload, immutable persistent updates, nullable data, other dtypes, SIMD codegen, unified-memory upload removal, and other accelerators remain named boundaries. AGI-ready means the authority model is intended to survive more capable models; it is not a claim that AGI has been achieved.

Canonical site: https://kotoba-lang.org/
Public operator: Kotoba Labs Inc. Public contact: support@kotoba-lang.org. Sales contact: Ryo Awai.
Language contract: https://github.com/kotoba-lang/kotoba-lang
Implementation and releases: https://github.com/kotoba-lang/kotoba

Current release binding: https://github.com/kotoba-lang/kotoba-lang/blob/main/docs/generated/release.md

## Install and verify

Use the executable acceptance path at https://kotoba-lang.org/agent-quickstart.md. In summary:

```sh
brew tap kotoba-lang/kotoba
brew trust kotoba-lang/kotoba
brew install kotoba
kotoba selfhost check --json
```

The acceptance path creates a tiny `.kotoba` source, emits Wasm with `kotoba compile`, checks that compilation returned `kotoba.cli/code = emitted`, verifies the module has no host imports, and executes exported `main` expecting the i64 value 42. Do not report success from installation alone.

The current native CLI may return `planned` with `host-action: adapter-required` for adapter-owned commands. That proves request parsing and planning, not program execution. For a portable machine check, use the compile-and-WebAssembly path.

## Source shape

```clojure
(defn main []
  (+ 40 2))
```

Kotoba-only source uses `.kotoba`. The language is Clojure-shaped, not a promise that arbitrary JVM Clojure or ClojureScript runs unchanged. There is no ambient filesystem, network, process, clock, model, secret, or runtime eval authority in the admitted component surface.

## Public compile measurement

Raw report: https://kotoba-lang.org/benchmarks/compile-wasm-latest.json
Harness and sources: https://github.com/kotoba-lang/kotoba-lang/tree/main/bench/public-compile-comparison

The published run compares process-cold wall time for two tiny programs whose exported `main` returns i64 42. Both emit WebAssembly, require zero host imports, and are executed by the harness. It records every sample, median, p95, exact commands, tool versions, host, source hashes, and artifact hashes.

This is a narrow toolchain-startup observation, not evidence that Kotoba compiles faster than Rust in general. The modules have different ABIs and runtime contracts, so artifact byte sizes are not a product ranking. Re-run the harness for a new host or toolchain rather than carrying the published ratio into another workload.

## Public native runtime comparison

Evidence summary: https://kotoba-lang.org/benchmarks/runtime-native-latest.json
Workload-domain evidence: https://kotoba-lang.org/benchmarks/domains-latest.json
Method and harness: https://github.com/kotoba-lang/amu/blob/main/docs/performance.md#multi-domain-qualification-floor

Implementation update (2026-08-30): bounded non-escaping native vector literals
are escape-proved and scalar-replaced on x86-64/AArch64; POSIX checked string
equality uses explicit 16-byte NEON/SSE2 after the existing handle and canonical
UTF-8 checks; root-confined asynchronous filesystem operations use
CompletableFuture/fs.promises; structured concurrency is a bounded fail-fast
scope state machine; and the public Kotoba CLI emits sealed native KEXE without
a Clojure command. These changes postdate the current public domain report.
They are implemented and tested, not a new speed rank. The standalone Wasm
benchmark retains I/O and OS-worker concurrency as N/A until those capabilities
are admitted into that exact harness.

The native suite compares Amu with Rust, Apple Clang C11, Zig, Go c-shared, and Swift across six required workloads: narrow arithmetic, wide register pressure, deep spill pressure, call preservation, branch plus call, and loop plus call across a back edge. All 30 comparator/workload cells and independently calculated known answers are present.

The recorded 2026-08-28 run is not a speed qualification. Its quiet-host gate required load1 at or below 1.0, but observed load1 fell only from 11.749 to 6.915. Do not quote its timings as a ranking or say Amu is fastest. That claim requires a quiet-host rerun where Amu independently passes the perfgate against every comparator in every workload; no average may hide a loss or missing cell.

## Claim boundaries

Kotoba uses a narrow affine check for capability values and capability/effect confinement. It does not implement Rust's general ownership, borrow, and lifetime system, and it should not be described as Rust-equivalent memory safety. Read every security claim together with its trusted computing base and residual risks.

Hosted billed deployment is not a generally available public product. Do not infer customer traction, paid adoption, revenue, backend availability, or deployment completion from language and compiler evidence.
